GEN-001.privatePlan: Invalid UTF-8, duplicate keys, surrogate escapes, numeric boundary spellings and exact UTC calendar cases across every request body.

GEN-002.privatePlan: Inject commit/disk/busy failures and check error envelope plus absence of effects; distinguish disconnect uncertainty.

GEN-003.privatePlan: Chunked input at each size boundary, malformed percent encoding, duplicated query keys and media/charset variants.

GEN-004.privatePlan: Cross-error priority matrices and controlled overlapping reader/writer schedules; no dirty/partial snapshot.

GEN-005.privatePlan: All wrong methods, route casing/trailing slashes, readiness during initialization and unavailable storage.

DATA-002.privatePlan: Restart with same database, failed initialization and changed fixture manifest; assert startup rejection without rewriting committed state.

CAT-001.privatePlan: All offset/limit boundaries, pagination over snapshot and empty fixture; concurrent inserts under documented cross-page semantics.

CAT-002.privatePlan: Intersect filters with zero/equal endpoints, all categories and active/discontinued distributions.

CAT-003.privatePlan: Large equal-key groups, numeric/string comparisons and descending primary with ascending secondary ID.

CAT-004.privatePlan: Imported/discontinued and absent IDs; reads before/after committed inventory changes.

INV-001.privatePlan: Missing/discontinued IDs, snapshot reads during writes, read consistency with catalogue.

INV-002.privatePlan: Upper/lower/zero bounds, failed commit and arithmetic overflow attempts; unchanged stock on all failures.

INV-003.privatePlan: Competing positive/negative adjustments and order writes; reconcile every success against final stock.

ORD-001.privatePlan: Maximum line/quantity counts, duplicate products with different quantities, exact line ordering/Location and temporal forms.

ORD-002.privatePlan: Sorted reference failure priority across multiple missing/inactive products and customer/duplicate-ID precedence.

ORD-003.privatePlan: Zero/high prices and totals at/above MAX_SAFE using independently computed integer ledger.

ORD-004.privatePlan: Late item failure, concurrent multi-product lock ordering, commit failure and reader snapshot isolation.

ORD-005.privatePlan: Duplicate IDs with changed payload, concurrent identical IDs, restart persistence and uncertain-response reconciliation.

ANA-001.privatePlan: Every timestamp boundary, invalid calendar date, snapshot overlap with writes and aggregate overflow.

ANA-002.privatePlan: Multiple historical lines/groups, zero revenue, no phantom failed orders and exact category snapshots.

ANA-003.privatePlan: Quantity/revenue/ID tie hierarchy, all limits, empty database/window and mixed write freshness.

IMP-001.privatePlan: 2 GiB wire, 2 million rows, exact 4096-byte line limits, every UTF-8 chunk split, CRLF, absent final LF and memory growth.

IMP-002.privatePlan: Each Product bound, missing/null/extra fields, Unicode scalar lengths and first invalid physical line.

IMP-003.privatePlan: Disconnect before EOF, late storage failure and readers during staged import; no partial records after rollback.

IMP-004.privatePlan: Concurrent overlapping ID/SKU sets and retry after lost success response, with no duplicate rows.

SIM-001.privatePlan: Every dimension/input bound, exact 4-billion operation cap and sorted missing-reference priority.

SIM-002.privatePlan: Independent cross-language random-word vectors including unsigned high bits, all coordinate axes and nonzero modulo cases.

SIM-003.privatePlan: Lead-time/reorder timing, single outstanding delivery, final-day pending events, stockout definition and demand conservation.

SIM-004.privatePlan: Exact half-up ties, zero demand, high intermediate integer products and deterministic parallel reductions.

SIM-005.privatePlan: Repeat/concurrent/permuted requests while stock changes; prove explicit simulation state and no persistent mutation.

SIM-006.privatePlan: Verify Medium/Large results independently outside timed phase; observe scaling without storing per-day objects.
